verdict.rationale: E2B documents a sandbox timeout that can be changed at runtime with setTimeout/set_timeout and reset to a new value. It also documents kill to shut a sandbox down before the timeout expires, which implies automatic shutdown when the timeout is reached. However, the evidence shows no idle/inactivity-based auto-shutdown and never states that billing stops when a sandbox times out; paused sandboxes are also kept indefinitely with no automatic deletion. missing for 10: inactivity-based (idle) auto-shutdown, explicit documentation that billing stops on timeout, a documented timeout parameter at sandbox creation, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, I can set timeouts so sandboxes shut down automatically and stop billing when idle or done

citations.quote: You can change the sandbox timeout when it's running by calling the `setTimeout` method in JavaScript or `set_timeout` method in Python.
When you call the set timeout method, the sandbox timeout will be reset to the new value that you specified.
You can shutdown the sandbox any time even before the timeout is up by calling the `kill` method.
